title: Is Baseboard, Kickplate & Corner Detailing Included in Standard Cleaning or Billed Extra?
seoTitle: Baseboard & Cubicle Corner Detailing: Included in Scope or Extra Charge?
metaDescription: Find out when cubicle deep vacuum and baseboard detailing is included in $0.07–$0.15/sq ft base retainers vs. billed at $55–$95/hr. Compare quotes now.
excerpt: Few scope gray areas cause more tension between office managers and janitorial contractors than dusty cubicle baseboards and scuffed door kickplates. Learn how to audit your cleaning contract's Scope of Work matrix to see what is included in your monthly retainer versus billed as an extra work order.
quickAnswer: In standard US commercial janitorial contracts ($0.05 to $0.20 per sq ft depending on building size), light dry dusting of accessible baseboards and rotational spot-vacuuming of visible cubicle corners are typically included on a monthly or quarterly cycle within multi-visit weekly retainers. However, moving under-desk pedestals to crevice-vacuum cable raceways, wet-scrubbing scuffed vinyl cove base, stripping yellowed VCT corner wax, and polishing metal door kickplates are almost universally billed as an extra add-on—either via a $0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month floor-care rider or a standalone work order at $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour.

blocks.text: The 'Wall-to-Wall Vacuuming' Clause: Why Tenant Expectations Clash with Vendor Math

Almost every dispute over dusty cubicle corners and scuffed baseboards traces back to a single vague line in a janitorial proposal: 'Vacuum all carpeted areas and damp-mop hard floors.' To a corporate office manager or facility director, 'all carpeted areas' means every square inch from partition wall to partition wall, including the 90-degree crevice under the desk pedestal, the metal cable raceway at the base of the cubicle panel, and the rubber cove baseboard behind the trash receptacle.

To a commercial janitorial estimator pricing a competitive bid at $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft (for a 10,000–24,999 sq ft floor) or $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft (for a 2,500–9,999 sq ft suite), that same clause is calculated using the ISSA open-floor production benchmark of 3,500 square feet per hour at a standard labor rate of $35 to $65 per hour. At 3,500 sq ft/hr, a technician with a 14-inch upright or backpack floor head walks continuous traffic lanes and reaches open under-desk knee wells. They do not have the allotted minutes to drop to their knees, detach the floor wand, fit a 1.5-inch crevice nozzle, move chair mats, or scrub heel marks off vinyl cove base and door kickplates.

blocks.text: When Detailing IS Included in Your Base Monthly Janitorial Retainer
You should expect basic crevice vacuuming and dry baseboard dusting to be folded into your base monthly price—without surprise extra invoices—under two specific contract structures:

items: High-Frequency Multi-Visit Retainers (3x to 5x Weekly): When you contract for 3x-weekly service (13.0 visits/month at a 0.95x multiplier) or 5x-weekly weekday service (21.65 visits/month at a 0.90x multiplier, based on 4.33 weeks/month), industry-standard Class A specifications include a 'Monthly or Quarterly Rotational Detail' column in the Scope of Work (SOW). Because daily soil is light, crews rotate through 25% of the building's baseboards and accessible cubicle corners each week as part of their base hours.

Day-Porter or Executive Suite Contracts: Facilities that employ a daytime porter or executive housekeeper equipped with a discreet mobile caddy—such as the Rubbermaid Commercial Executive Quick Cart Large (featuring a 60 lb capacity, Teflon-coated fabric protector, quiet casters, and stealth charcoal appearance for Class A lobbies and executive tours)—routinely include daily or weekly spot-wiping of lobby door kickplates, conference room baseboards, and glass partition tracks ($15 to $35/visit interior glass benchmark) during off-peak daytime hours.

blocks.text: When Vendors Legitimately Charge Extra (Project Work Orders vs. Monthly Riders)
Conversely, a janitorial contractor is operating entirely within standard US commercial norms when they issue a separate add-on quote for restorative edge work. Four scenarios justify an extra bill:

First, low-frequency general contracts—such as monthly (1.0 visit/mo, 1.28x multiplier), biweekly (2.17 visits/mo, 1.16x multiplier), or 1x-weekly (4.33 visits/mo, 1.08x multiplier) service—only budget enough technician hours per visit to empty trash, sanitize restrooms ($15 to $30 per restroom per visit), wipe breakrooms ($12 to $25 per visit), and run high-speed open-lane floor passes. Adding deep cubicle corner extraction requires extra labor hours at $35 to $65/hr (or triggers a $90 to $135 minimum visit charge if scheduled separately).

Second, wet chemical edge restoration on hard flooring carries real material and specialty labor costs. If your suite features VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x multiplier), engineered hardwood (1.08x multiplier), or ceramic tile and grout (1.12x multiplier) with darkened acrylic wax build-up or calcified restroom cove grout, a technician must use chemical strippers, scraping tools, and orbital edge scrubbers billed at $55 to $95 per specialty hour.

Third, initial move-in or onboarding remediation is never free. If a newly hired janitorial vendor inherits 18 months of compacted dust bunnies under 100 cubicles from a terminated contractor, they will bill a one-time 'Initial Deep Detail Clean' before maintaining the suite under the regular monthly retainer.

blocks.title: Contract Language Red Flag: 'As Needed' vs. 'Quarterly Rotational'
blocks.text: Never sign a janitorial Scope of Work that lists baseboard wiping, kickplate polishing, or corner detail vacuuming under an 'As Needed' column. In commercial contract enforcement, 'As Needed' is legally unenforceable and defaults to zero scheduled hours. Demand an explicit calendar frequency column: '1x Monthly (Rotational 25%/wk)' or '4x Annually (Quarterly).'
Operational Setup That Makes Rotational Inclusion Viable for Your Crew

Often, evening cleaners skip included rotational edge detailing simply because fetching a crevice nozzle or damp baseboard cloth from a distant basement closet wastes 15 minutes of walking. Well-managed contracts specify on-floor equipment staging so detail tools travel directly with the waste and vacuum collector.

When the nightly trash and vacuum runner utilizes a 44-gallon barrel outfitted with a Rubbermaid Commercial Brute Rim Caddy Attachment (providing 9 snap-on compartments and integrated tool clips for crevice wands, microfiber cloths, and neutral spray bottles), the technician can spot-detail scuffed kickplates and dusty corner junctions in real time without backtracking. Similarly, replacing small, tip-prone desk cans around high-spill copy rooms and breakroom corridors with a heavy-base Simplehuman 55L / 14.5-Gal Commercial Semi-Round Open Can (14.5-gallon brushed stainless steel, ADA-friendly open top) prevents the daily coffee and food splashes that turn standard dry baseboard dusting into an extra-charge wet scrubbing project.
How to Negotiate Baseboard and Cubicle Detailing Before Signing an RFP

items.name: Insert a Separate Line Item in Your RFP Scope Matrix
items.text: Break 'Vacuuming & Floor Care' into two distinct rows on your bid sheet: Row A for 'Traffic-Lane & Knee-Well HEPA Vacuuming (Per Visit)' and Row B for 'Cubicle Raceway Crevice Vacuum, Baseboard Damp Wipe & Door Kickplate Detail (Quarterly / Monthly Rotation).'

items.name: Request Both Bundled and Standalone Add-On Pricing
items.text: Instruct bidders to show the base monthly retainer PLUS the exact cost of adding the Quarterly Deep Floor Care rider ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo) versus ordering edge detailing a la carte ($0.04–$0.12/sq ft per event). Vendors competing for a 12-month contract will frequently waive or halve the quarterly detailing fee to win the base retainer.

items.name: Define Furniture & Cable Boundaries in Writing
items.text: Clarify in the contract that cleaners will move rolling task chairs and floor mats to detail corners, while stationary lateral files and heavy IT cabling bundlers will be detailed around with a narrow crevice wand without disconnecting hardware.

faqs.q: Can I withhold payment if my janitorial crew leaves dusty baseboards on a standard contract?
faqs.a: Only if your signed Scope of Work (SOW) explicitly lists baseboard and corner detailing under a defined frequency column (such as Weekly, Monthly, or Quarterly). If your contract only states 'vacuum carpets and dust horizontal desk surfaces,' baseboards and cubicle raceways are technically outside the base scope. In that case, use your next contract renewal or quarterly review to add a formal rotational schedule.

faqs.q: What is the price difference between an amortized monthly rider and a one-off work order?
faqs.a: An amortized Quarterly Deep Floor Care rider typically adds $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month to your base invoice and bundles edge detailing with periodic carpet extraction or hard-floor buffing. Ordering the same detailing as a standalone one-off work order usually costs 15% to 30% more per event because the vendor bills specialty hourly rates ($55–$95/hr) plus administrative dispatch overhead.

faqs.q: Are paper and chemical consumables for baseboard detailing billed extra?
faqs.a: Cleaning chemicals, microfiber pads, and HEPA vacuum bags used by the janitorial crew are standard contractor overhead and should always be included in their hourly or per-square-foot labor rate. Don't confuse contractor cleaning chemicals with tenant restroom/breakroom consumables (toilet tissue, hand towels, soap, and can liners), which are billed separately at $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit when vendor-supplied.

faqs.q: Who pays for lobby door kickplate and corridor baseboard detailing in a multi-tenant building?
faqs.a: In a multi-tenant commercial office building, common-area ground-floor lobbies, elevator banks, and shared stairwell kickplates are maintained by the landlord's building janitorial crew and billed back to tenants proportionally through Common Area Maintenance (CAM) charges. Everything inside your leased suite demising walls—including your suite entry door kickplate and interior cubicles—falls under your tenant janitorial contract unless you have a full-service gross lease.

faqs.q: How many hours should a contractor allocate to detail baseboards and cubicles in a 10,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: For a standard 10,000 sq ft office with 60 to 80 modular cubicles and mixed carpet/VCT flooring, a thorough quarterly crevice vacuum, damp baseboard wipe, and kickplate polish requires roughly 10 to 15 total labor hours (650 to 1,000 gross sq ft per hour). At $35 to $65 per standard labor hour, the fair market labor value is $350 to $975 per quarterly cycle.
